name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: Trump, Xi and Putin discussed nuclear arms cuts in Shenzhen on 19 Nov; no deal found, New START limits still lapsed
state: At a three-way meeting in Shenzhen on 19 Nov, Trump said the US, China and Russia were uniquely positioned to discuss reducing nuclear weapons (CNBC); France 24 reported the leaders agreed a nuclear war must never be fought. No arms-control agreement was found, and US–Russia treaty limits have been absent since New START expired in February. No test, alert change or threatened use was found as of 19 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No official guidance change. The lapse of treaty limits is a long-running condition rather than an immediate threat.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse (New START, Feb) without replacement

sources.title: CNBC — Trump: U.S., China, Russia uniquely positioned to discuss reducing nuclear weapons
France 24 — Trump, Xi and Putin agree that a nuclear war must never be fought

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
